subject: forestSpirit
pitch: A small forest spirit, part deer and part mossy stone. A body of grey river stone covered in soft green moss, slender wooden legs ending in little hooves, branching antlers sprouting tiny white flowers and leaves, a pale wooden mask-like face with two glowing green eyes, and a few fireflies circling its head.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the proportions for a deer-sized spirit creature, roughly 1.1m body length and 0.9m shoulder height, with antlers reaching up to about 1.5m, and starting to plan the joint hierarchy beginning with hips as the root.

Now I'm mapping out the skeletal structure in detail: pelvis as root, with a chain through chest, neck, and head, then separate leg chains (hip, knee, ankle, hoof) for each limb, using capsule shapes between joints to form the slender wooden legs and stony body segments.

I'm planning the stone body using low-poly dodecahedron shapes with a mottled grey stone texture blended with mossy green patches based on surface normal direction and noise, so moss appears naturally on upward-facing surfaces.

I'm positioning the body with scale and bone attachment at the chest, working out the extents so legs and neck join cleanly without awkward gaps, then placing the neck and head with a pale wooden mask-like face.

For the head I'm shaping a flat box as a mask with pale wood tones, adding small bright green spheres for glowing eyes since true emissive isn't available, then starting on antlers as branching rod shapes swept along curved paths from the brow outward.

Still planning antler geometry...

For leaves I'll use tiny green icosahedrons, and mirror the whole antler setup for the right side with a sign-flipping function. I'll scatter a handful of small emissive yellow-green firefly spheres circling around the head joint, then move on to building slender wooden legs with hoof caps.

Each leg gets a hip-knee-ankle-hoof capsule chain with dark cylindrical hooves, named by front/back and left/right combinations (hipFL, kneeFL, ankleFL, hoofFL, etc.), wired together as joints with proper parent references and grouped into leg chains with a "leg" role.

Rather than wrestle with chain internals further, I decide it's simpler and more reliable to use b.joint directly for the legs, reserving b.chain for the spine where the parent/path semantics are clearer.

I'm sketching the rest of the rig: spine joints with explicit parent set to pelvis and role labels for spine, neck, and head, a small moss-covered tail stub instead of a full chain, scattered stone dodecahedrons on the back for texture, and painted moss/leaf details on the antlers and body using the paint-wrapped colors, plus the necessary THREE and builder imports.

Now I'm defining the actual material palette — mottled stone and moss paints blended by a noise-based coverage function, wood grain paints for antlers, legs, and hooves, and a pale grain mask for the face — all using the mottle, grain, and noise helpers with specific seeds and colors.

Setting up the builder's joint hierarchy next: pelvis, chest, neck, and head joints each positioned relative to their parent, confirming that explicit parent joints correctly inherit rotation and that role labels like "spine", "neck", and "head" tag them for the rig. Then I'm attaching the main dodecahedron body part to the chest bone with mossy paint and a flattened, non-uniform scale to shape the torso.

Now I'm defining a reusable leg-building function that generates hip, knee, ankle, and hoof joints for front and back legs on each side, naming them with side/position tags like hipFL or ankleBR, and working out plausible 3D coordinates so front knees bend forward slightly and back legs bend backward like a deer's hock.

Then I'm chaining these joints into a leg skeleton and building capsule meshes between each joint pair (hip-to-knee, knee-to-ankle, etc.), with the hoof itself as a small cylinder sitting near the ground.

Still defining chain joints and head geometry...

Checking the eye placement against the mask's curved surface to make sure they protrude slightly without sinking in, then setting the eye color to a light green.

Now I'm sketching out the antlers: small spheres for the eyes, then sweeping tapered beams from a base point on the head outward and upward through a few control points on each side, shrinking the radius toward the tips.

I'm adding branches off the beams using rod segments with their own tapered radii, plus small icosahedron shapes for leaves and flower buds scattered along the antlers and at the branch ends.

Now I'm placing a handful of firefly points floating near the head, computing their positions in a loop with slightly varied angles and radii so they orbit around the figure organically.

Finally, I'm adding a mossy tuft detail near the back and double-checking the leg and hoof placements so everything rests cleanly on the ground, then wrapping the whole construction inside the default export function that returns the finished root.

Writing the stone and moss paint definitions...

Still building skeleton joints...

Adding a tail tuft, then setting up a leg-building function that computes bone chains for front/back legs with mirrored left/right offsets.

Still verifying leg joint structure...

For the neck and head, I'm placing a capsule tube from chest to neck on the chest bone, then adding a dodecahedron head part attached to the neck bone with slight scale distortion for a more organic shape. The neck tube won't bend independently since it's weighted to the chest bone, but that's acceptable since the head itself moves separately via the neck joint.

For the mask and eyes, I'm positioning a flattened sphere on the head bone to form a mask shape in front of the dodecahedron face, then adding two small glowing spheres as eyes symmetrically placed on either side using a mirrored offset. I'm skipping a nose or mouth detail for now.

Starting the antlers, I'm defining a sweep function that builds a curved horn shape from a series of points mirrored by side, tapering from a thicker base to a narrow tip using varying radii.

Still writing antler branches...

Now I'm placing white flower blooms along the antler tips and beam, plus leaf shapes with octahedron geometry and slight rotation for a natural look. I'm also scattering fireflies around the head using a loop with varying angle and radius, placing them in model-space coordinates relative to the head bone.

I'm double-checking that types match across all the part options -- scale, rotation, and position all accept vector-like arrays, and the mottle/names options conform to their expected shapes. Everything looks consistent, so I'll finalize the structure and return the root without additional commentary.
